title: My God! How Perfect Are Thy Ways
description: My God! How Perfect Are Thy Ways in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 67, “Jehovah our righteousness. Jer 23:6”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God! how per-fect are thy ways! But mine pol-lut-ed are; Sin twines it-self a-bout my praise, And slides in-to my prayer.

lines: My God! how perfect are thy ways!
Sin twines itself about my praise,
When I would speak what thou hast done
To save me from my sin;
I cannot make thy mercies known
This heart, a fountain of vile thoughts,
While self upon the surface floats
Let others in the gaudy dress
The Lord shall be my righteousness

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
